full_judgment: 2. Facts relevant are that the Head Master of the Olympia Textile Mills High School and a guardian of a student studying in that school as petitioners preferred the writ petition seeking a direction upon the writ respondents to comply with the "Transfer of State Owned textile Mills to Workers and Employees (procedure and Term and Conditions) Guidelines, 2000" dated 10.02.2000 by allowing the Olympia Textile Mills High School continuing and functioning in its existing premises situated within the erstwhile Olympia Textile Mills ltd. Monno Nagar , P.S - Tongi, Gazipur, contending interalia, that Olympia Textile Mills High School (hereinafter referred as 'the High School') was established as a Non-Govornment School in 1974 on 3 acres of land in Plot Nos.93-94, Khatian No.13, Mouza: Masimpur, Monno Nagar, Police Station-Tongi, District-Gazipur within the premises of the erstwhile Olympia Textile Mills Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Mill') a state owned textile mill managed by the Bangladesh Textile Mills Corporation (hereinafter referred as the BTMC') Government recognized the School in 1981 and since 2001 the High School has been receiving Monthly payment Order (MPO) from the Government. The High School has over 700 students having highest pass rates in Gazipur in SSC examination. Originally, the High School catered for the educational needs of the children of mill workers but now it also served the educational needs of the local children who belong to low income workers in that area. The Olympia Textile Mills was nationalized along with other mills as per provision of P.O No.27 of 1972. Over the next 28 years the mills along with other nationalized mills become loss making enterprises which ultimately had to be shut down. In such situation, in exercise of the power conferred by Article 4(2) of P.O No.27 of 1972 the Government framed "Transfer of State Owned Textile Mills to Workers and Employees (Procedure and Terms and conditions) Guidelines, 2000" dated 10.02.2000 (hereinafter referred to as the Guidelines') by Gazette Notification dated 10.02.2000. Under the terms and conditions of the Guidelines, it was deter-mined amongst others, that the mill be transformed to a company formed by the mill workers so that they could be operated more efficiently. The mill had 41.81 acres of land of which 15.10 acres were identified for transfer to the company to be formed by the workers of the mill. The rest 26.71 acres were identified as excess land. The 3 (three) acres of land werein the High School is situated is located within the excess land. Note 2 to the Schedule 2 of the Guidelines has stated that educational institutions, religious places, water pumps, overhead tanks, electric stations etc. would be reserved for the use of all concerned. Thus the High School is entitled to continue its existence on the land upon which it is situated. But the BTMC in gross violation of the Guidelines sold the excess 26.71 acres of land including the 3 acres of land on which the High School is situated to the writ-respondent No.8.
